evidenceSpecTemplate.minOpenLeadSecondsNote: DERIVED FLOOR + OWNER CHOICE. Floor: must be strictly greater than maxFutureSkewSeconds (30), or an admissible print for the target can already exist when the Need opens and the settling price is knowable before the shot is committed. Enforced by lib.rs::validate_spec; proved in lifecycle.rs::lead_above_skew_is_exactly_the_condition_for_an_unknowable_price. The floor is arithmetic; the VALUE is taste. Was 30, which equalled the skew and could not register. Set to one full grid (60) so a player commits at least a whole round ahead, with 29 s of margin over the floor. The bare minimum that registers is 31. Both are one line and neither needs a proof - this is the owner's call.
evidenceSpecTemplate.targetGridSecondsNote: OWNER DECISION, AND IT IS NOW THE ONLY PARAMETER THE SLOW FEEDS ARE SENSITIVE TO. The lag is derived (grid - 1 = 59) and is already MAXIMAL - it cannot be raised without letting one print settle two consecutive targets. So the only lever left is this number. Measured, docs/reviews/cadence/cadence-2026-09-05.summary.json, WIDEST OBSERVED publish gap per feed (not p99 - for a write-once parameter the tail is the whole risk): SOL 7 s, BTC 7 s, JUP 53 s, BONK 54 s, PUMP 54 s, ETH 55 s, WIF 58 s. At grid 60 the lag is 59, so WIF has 1 SECOND of margin before a target finds no admissible print and VOIDs. At grid 300 the lag is 299 and the same feed has 241 s of margin. SOL and BTC are comfortable either way. A void is a full refund and is the correct outcome when no evidence exists - it is not a fault - but a one-second margin on five of seven feeds is a game that voids often, permanently, because register_economy cannot be edited. The honest options are: grid 300 for everything; grid 60 for SOL/BTC and 300 for the slow five; or launch SOL/BTC only. This is a question about what the game IS, not about what is true.

launchScope.ownerStatementMeaning: Asked to choose between (A) SOL and BTC only at grid 60 and (C) all seven feeds at grid 300 for every feed, the owner answered 'svih sedam' - all seven. That is option C. The grid is part of what he chose, because option C was stated to him as 'all seven, grid 300 for all'. Recorded here as his words plus this reading of them, so that nothing is attributed to him that he did not say.
launchScope.whyOneGridAndNotTwo: A mixed launch - grid 60 for SOL/BTC and 300 for the slow five - was considered and rejected before he was asked. It buys the extra tokens by creating two economies inside one: at grid 300 a player gets 80% fewer rounds per day and therefore 80% fewer chances at XP, so the slow feeds would be dead weight on a shared daily leaderboard. Nobody had analysed that fairness, and these numbers are written once. One grid is a rule; two grids is an exception with an unexamined consequence.
launchScope.marginEvidence: Widest observed gap between consecutive publishes, 63-minute mainnet run, all 7 feeds, 442 targets, zero RPC errors (docs/reviews/cadence/cadence-2026-09-05.summary.json): SOL 7 s, BTC 7 s, JUP 53 s, BONK 54 s, PUMP 54 s, ETH 55 s, WIF 58 s. At grid 300 the lag is 299, so the tightest feed (WIF) has 241 s of margin before a target finds no admissible print. At grid 60 that same feed had 1 s.
launchScope.knownLimitOfThatEvidence: 63 minutes is not a tail characterisation. It is the reason for choosing the grid with 241 s of margin rather than the one with 1 s, not a claim that the tail is known.
launchScope.horizonCheck: horizon_seconds % target_grid_seconds == 0 for all seven horizons (300, 600, 900, 1800, 3600, 21600, 86400) at grid 300.

permanentCosts._: COSTS THAT ARE NEVER REFUNDED IN THIS GENERATION. Written here because a player pays them and must be able to find them before playing, not discover them afterwards. Every number below is DERIVED from a constant in source; none of it is a proposal or a judgement.
permanentCosts.needRentDerivation: TimepinNeedV2::LEN = 160 (onchain/rcx-timepin-v2/.../lib.rs), account = 8 + 160 = 168 bytes. Solana rent exemption = (128 + data_len) * 3480 * 2 = 296 * 6960 = 2,060,160 lamports.
permanentCosts.needRentPaidBy: Whoever calls open_need. It is init_if_needed with payer = actor, and the Need is SHARED per (spec, target_ts), so the cost is per TARGET ACTUALLY PLAYED - not per grid slot.
permanentCosts.needRentWhyPermanent: There is no close_need and there must not be one yet. The field it would be guarded by, open_refs, is written to zero at open_need and never incremented anywhere - the guard open_refs == 0 is 0 == 0. A Need is shared and closing deletes the account that settle_final and the void path both read, so one permissionless close on that vacuous guard would strand every shot on that target permanently. A retention timer cannot substitute: settlement assigns reveal_deadline_ts = max(now + reveal_window, projection), so a shot's life has no upper bound computable from the Need. The real fix is hold_need/release_need with Core calling both, which requires Timepin to decide who may hold - an architectural change for a later generation.
permanentCosts.needRentUpperBoundNote: At grid 300 a fully played day is 86400/300 = 288 targets per feed, so one feed accrues 288 * 2,060,160 = 593,326,080 lamports = 0.593 SOL/day = 216.6 SOL/year, and all seven feeds come to 1,516 SOL/year. That is the FULLY PLAYED upper bound, not an expected cost. For comparison, the earlier grid-60 proposal cost 1,083 SOL/year PER FEED: two feeds at grid 60 would have been 2,166 SOL/year. Choosing grid 300 therefore added five tokens AND cut the permanent rent ceiling by 30% against a two-feed launch.

needsInFlight.note: At grid 60 this was 1,500 simultaneous open targets, a number flagged as unjustified when the manifest was first drafted. The grid decision reduced it fivefold without anyone editing it.

knownMismatches.whyItMatters: They govern different gates but they meet: the ruleset decides when a player may open a shot, the evidence spec decides when a Need may be opened for the target. If a shot can be opened at a lead the Need cannot, the shot has no evidence to settle against.
knownMismatches.status: UNRESOLVED - flagged, not silently reconciled. An economic parameter is not changed by whoever notices it.
knownMismatches.owner: GeminiForge to trace both to source; Semir to decide if they must differ.
